lessons.old:
## The take column moves, and that is the trap

Take rises as the interest falls: 66.1723 percent at 100, 79.7034 at 60, 91.5431 at 25. The regime has not changed. What changed is that the engine's take compares the partner's scaled net cash flow with the field's unscaled pre-take value, so at 25 percent the number reads as the share of the field's value that this partner does not keep, which includes the other partners as much as the government. Quoting 91.5431 percent as the fiscal take of a 25 percent interest misreads the column; the government's share of the field is the 66.1723 percent on the 100 percent row, whatever interest is held.
lessons.new:
## What the take used to do

Until the 2026-09-15 repair the JV ledger was the odd regime out. It kept gross revenue, volumes and costs at field level while reporting royalty, tax and net cash flow at the share, so take compared a partner's scaled net with the field's unscaled value and rose as the interest fell: 74.6292 percent at 75, 79.7034 at 60, 86.4689 at 40 and 91.5431 at 25. Those numbers are history. A take that moves with the interest is a reading about the partnership and not about the government.

lessons.old:
## The mistake

The careful mistake is to trust the residual as a proof of uniqueness. A residual of 0.000000 at 173.6932 percent proves that 173.6932 is a root; it says nothing about the interval from -75 to -50, where the same curve crosses zero again. The finder reports the root it reached, and its statement does not say which root that is when there are several.
lessons.new:
## What it used to do

Until engines 3.10.0 the finder's statement read "Newton now falls back to bisection when unconverged and returns null when no sign change brackets a root", and said nothing about how many roots there were. On this vector it reported 173.6932 percent, the crossing Newton reached from 10 percent, with the one near -73.6932 unmentioned.

## The mistake

The careful mistake is to trust a residual as a proof of uniqueness. A residual of 0.000000 proves that the rate beside it is a root, and says nothing about the rest of the curve. The engine does that counting now: a named rate means one crossing was found in the band.
lessons.why: EC1-2: the engine names a rate only where exactly one rate in the band -99 to 1000 percent zeroes the NPV, and otherwise returns null with an irrStatus (no-sign-change, no-root, above-clamp, multiple-roots with the roots listed). It no longer reports whichever root Newton reached. The defect is now taught as history alongside what the engine does.

lessons.old: It refuses to return an unconverged Newton estimate: the fallback runs instead. It refuses to bisect without a bracket, and when no sign change is found it returns null rather than a guess. And it refuses to count roots, so a converged answer is one answer, not the answer.
lessons.new: It refuses to return an unconverged Newton estimate: the fallback runs instead. It refuses to bisect without a bracket, reporting null with irrStatus no-root or no-sign-change. It refuses to name a rate when the band holds several, and it refuses to look outside -99 to 1000 percent, flagging a crossing above the top as above-clamp.
lessons.why: "It refuses to count roots" is exactly what the repair reversed: the engine counts roots now.

lessons.old:
## The profile point at the applied rate

The NPV profile is reported at 0, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15 and 20 percent plus the applied rate, and the header says the applied point always passes through the headline NPV. On the nominal basis it does: jv_analytic_decision_kpis reads 21590909.09 at 10 percent against a headline of 21590909.09, gap 0.00. On the real basis the applied rate is the Fisher rate, 6.796117 percent, and the profile point is evaluated at that rate rounded to two decimals, 6.8.
lessons.new:
## The payback of a field that ends underwater

Payback reports the first year in which the cumulative cash flow turns non-negative, and it never looks again. AKATA with a 200000000 lump sum in 2035 reports payback 3.46 years, which is exactly what the run with no abandonment at all reports, while its nominal flows sum to -58362170.82 at 0 percent, its NPV is -40359955.35 at the applied rate and its IRR is null. A field that ends with less than it started reads as paid back in its fourth year. Distrust a payback until the sign of the last row and the total beneath it have been read beside it.
lessons.why: EC1-1 labels the applied-rate profile point at the rounded rate and evaluates it at the exact rate, so it is the headline and the gap is 0.00. The first of the three numbers is repaired, so the slot now teaches a defect that survives: payback ignores a later re-crossing.

lessons.old:
## The IRR of a profile with two roots

The vector [-100, 208, -108.12] has an NPV of -0.120000 at 0 percent, -0.000000 at 2, 0.036982 at 4, 0.000000 at 6 and -0.102881 at 8. Two rates zero it. The engine reports 6.0000 percent; the oracle reports 2.0000. Both answer the question, and the header does not say which root is returned when there are several. The method statement does: Newton from 10 percent, so the root nearer 10 is found.

## The allowance flag that reports one cap of two

computeProductionAllowance limits the per-barrel allowance twice: by the lease rate, and by pia_production_allowance_pct_of_price 20 of the year's price. Only the second limit is ever flagged. A converted lease lifting 1000000 bbl earns 2500000.00 at 80 USD/bbl and 2000000.00 at 10 USD/bbl, where the price limit cut it, and prod_alw_cap_applied reads false on both rows. The flag turns true only where the volume cap acted, as it does for a new shallow water lease at a prior cumulative of 99500000, which earns 4000000.00 on 500000.00 eligible bbl. Distrust a false flag read as a statement that no cap acted.
lessons.why: EC1-2 names a rate only where exactly one rate in the band from -99 to 1000 percent zeroes the NPV, and otherwise returns null with a status. The second of the three numbers is repaired, so the slot now teaches a defect that survives: prod_alw_cap_applied reports the volume cap only.

The fund contribution is scaled by working interest and the lump sum is not: 15000000.00 collected against 30000000.00 reported on the fund, 10000000.00 charged in full against 60 percent flows on the lump sum. lessons.new:
## The allowance beside its own eligible barrels

AKATA under the PIA at a 50 percent working interest reports a production allowance of 2750000.00 on 2200000.00 eligible bbl. The allowance is the share, halved with every other monetary line. The eligible barrels are the field's, because the tier and the volume cap have to be read on the field. Two bases sit in one row and nothing says so. pia_deep_offshore_wi_50 does the same at a larger scale, 27375000.00 of allowance beside 21900000.00 eligible bbl. Distrust any per-barrel rate got by dividing one of those columns by the other.
lessons.why: EC1-3 grosses the abandonment fund by one over the working interest, so abandonment_cost_usd is the share under both funding modes. The third of the three numbers is repaired, so the slot now teaches a defect that survives: a share-level allowance printed beside field-level eligible barrels.
